questions.stem: Why do root hair cells have a long, thin extension?

options.text: To increase their surface area for absorbing water and mineral ions from the soil
To anchor the plant more firmly in the ground
To store extra glucose produced by the plant

questions.explanation: The long, thin hair-like extension of root hair cells greatly increases the surface area in contact with soil particles, allowing the cell to absorb water by osmosis and mineral ions by active transport more efficiently.
